newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies seen lower on lower cash.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies seen lower on lower cash.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent per lb lower and pork bellies were called 0.200 to 0.500 cent a lb lower, livestock analysts said.

Lower cash hog indications on expected light packer demand ahead of the holiday were expected to weigh on hog futures. Packers have adequate live supplies to meet kill needs through the holiday weekend and lower cash pork prices will also keep packer bids down, analysts said.
Cooler weather is also allowing easier movement of hogs to market, they said.

Pork belly futures were expected to show carryover selling interest following a weak tone to cash bellies. Cash belly prices again hit resistance after trading up to $90 per cwt earlier in the week as user interest dried up at the higher price level.
Hog slaughter is also running above a year ago which is offsetting support from low stored stocks, they said.
Trading in both pits is expected to be on the light side and possibly choppy ahead of the long Independence Day holiday weekend, they added.
There will be normal trading hours Thursday.
